card werk-stack-ui  [decided]
The client builds its screens from shadcn/ui components
why: An agent writes most of the client. It writes faster and more consistently when it picks from a small set of known components than when it styles each screen by hand. shadcn/ui is the React component set that agents know best, and the client owns its source, so a change is a plain edit.

To keep screens consistent and cheap for an agent to write, the client builds every button, input, dialog, menu, tab, tooltip and layout from one component set: shadcn/ui. Each component is a Radix primitive, which gives keyboard focus, roles and screen reader labels, styled with Tailwind. React support comes from #werk-stack-framework.

The component files are copied into the client as its own source, not installed as a package. So the set is small and fixed, each component has a documented contract, and a change to a component's look or behaviour is an edit to one file, not a fork of a library. Tailwind compiles to static CSS, so no style work runs in the browser on each render.

To keep the set from drifting, a screen changes a component only through its variants and its class names. A new look that more than one screen needs becomes a new variant in the shared component file. A screen never edits a shared component for its own case.

  -> refines         werk-stack  The frontend needs a component stack
  -> depends_on      werk-stack-framework  Client framework: React + Vite
       why: The component system must support React, the framework that #werk-stack-framework chose.
  <- alternative_to  werk-stack-ui:opt1  Radix Themes: a fixed set of styled components, set through props and CSS variables
  <- alternative_to  werk-stack-ui:opt2  Mantine: a large styled library with CSS modules
  <- alternative_to  werk-stack-ui:opt3  MUI or Chakra: styled libraries that compute styles in JavaScript
Options
  werk-stack-ui:opt1  Radix Themes: a fixed set of styled components, set through props and CSS variables
    why not: Its set is small and its contract is strict, but a look outside its props needs a CSS override against styles the client does not own. Agents also know it less well than shadcn/ui, so they guess more about its props.
  werk-stack-ui:opt2  Mantine: a large styled library with CSS modules
    why not: It styles with static CSS, but its set is large and comes with its own hooks for forms and hotkeys. An agent then has several ways to build the same screen, which defeats a small fixed set.
  werk-stack-ui:opt3  MUI or Chakra: styled libraries that compute styles in JavaScript
    why not: Both compute styles in JavaScript on each render, through Emotion. That costs time on every render and fails the static CSS criterion. MUI also has a very large component set.

card werk-stack-framework  [decided]
Client framework: React + Vite
why: Criterion 2 (state-preserving per-component HMR) and criterion 6 (agent proficiency) both point at React, and neither runner-up wins them back.

React + Vite. Vite runs as the CLIENT dev server, in middleware mode, inside werk's own Bun server. It is not the server runtime — that is why this does not contradict #werk-hmr, which rejected **vite-node as the process host** after it crashed werk outright (#werk-hmr:src2). One process: Bun serves the API and the SSE stream and hot-reloads its own modules. Vite transforms and hot-reloads the client.

## Why, against the six criteria

1. **Component architecture** — React. Every candidate satisfied this.
2. **Per-component HMR preserving state** — the discriminator. React Fast Refresh preserves hook state per component. It is the most proven implementation of this requirement. Every rejected option lost or weakened it: Lit has no equivalent (#werk-stack:opt0), Solid remounts (#werk-stack:opt2), svelte-hmr is less reliable for the case that matters (#werk-stack:opt3). werk's chat pane holds a live SSE stream and an in-flight turn. Partly. You reach it in two hops, and the first hop is a `depends_on` edge, not a child edge.

```
#werk  ──depends_on──▶  #werk-stack  ◀──refines──  #werk-stack-ui
                             │
                             └──refines──▶  #visual
```

1. `#werk` has no `refines` path to `#werk-stack-ui`. The card sits under `#visual`, by way of `#werk-stack`.
2. `#werk` lists `#werk-stack` as a dependency, and its body names `#werk-stack` too. The only way down from `#werk` is to follow that link, then open the sub-cards of `#werk-stack`.
3. The body of `#werk` does not name the component set or `#werk-stack-ui`.

So a reader who looks only at the sub-cards of `#werk` does not find it.

There are two ways to fix it, if you want one:
- **Move it (recommended):** move `#werk-stack` so that it sits under `#werk`. Then the whole stack subtree is under `#werk`, and the card is two levels below it. This changes where `#werk-stack` sits in the map.
- **Link it:** add a `depends_on` edge from `#werk` to `#werk-stack-ui`. The card then shows on `#werk` directly. This adds an edge that `#werk-stack` already covers.

werk v0
why: The smallest visual layer over Claude Code that I can use while building it.
subtree: 20 cards, 20 decided, 2 unchallenged

What v0 contains. Each item is a concept elsewhere on the map; this card only says it is in v0. A depends_on edge to each item records the inclusion.

- The chat pane beside the map: #werk-chat.
- The CLI as the only write path, with remove and find: #werk-write.
- Extracted excerpts: #werk-excerpt.
- Card rendering: #werk-reflink, #werk-codeblock.
- The wording rule for card text: #werk-wording.
- Reopen reasons in the staleness view: #reopen-reason-gap.
- New cards as proposals: #werk-propose-new.
- The contract check at decided: #werk-contract.
- The dev loop and the Bun runtime: #werk-dev, #werk-hmr.
- The test harness: #werk-test.
- The ticket board: #werk-board.
- Multichat: #werk-mc-scope.
- The inner build loop: #werk-loop.
- Alignment before building: #align.

The core of v0 is three views: the map, the board, and the chat. The product diagram, the 3D graph, and the Flow view are outside v0. So are the tracker export, the validate stage, and pipeline self-measurement.

v0 is a new project in its own repository, built from scratch on #werk-stack (#werk-base). The log, the fold, and the web view are the three parts. Bun runs the server TypeScript directly (#werk-hmr). Vite transforms the client.

I staged a rewording of `#werk-stack`. It waits for your ✓ on the card.

`#werk-stack` was the unclear card. It read as a one-time v0 rewrite, not as the general shape of the product:
- **Old title:** "The frontend needs a component stack".
- **Old why:** "The current frontend is 2422 lines of hand-rolled rendering… the replacement".
- **Old body:** it began with "A new implementation is built on this stack from scratch — not a migration plan".

The proposal changes it like this:
- **Title:** "werk's client is built from components on one framework".
- **Why:** hand-written rendering grows with every screen, and each screen solves layout, state and live updates its own way. A component framework gives every screen one way to do this, so an agent changes one small part at a time.
- **Body:** the general rule. It points to `#werk-stack-framework`, `#werk-stack-hydration`, `#werk-hmr` and `#werk-stack-api`. It has no rewrite story and no table of child cards.

`#werk` stays as it is. Its dependency on `#werk-stack` is correct. So you find `#werk-stack-ui` under `#visual` → `#werk-stack`, not under `#werk`.

Next: open `#werk-stack`, read the diff, and press ✓ or discard it.
